description:
Split out of op-uyi3 (2026-08-13). op-uyi3 proposed promoting the golden-section search into outram-foam-basic-lib::math::minimise. The local de-duplication was done; the promotion was NOT, because it collides with an unstated architectural fact:

tampines-steam-tables ALREADY contains outram-foam-basic-lib, vendored as source. crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/openfoam_source/ is 101 files / 23489 lines of it, and src/openfoam_algorithms/CLAUDE.md documents the vendoring as deliberate ('do not attempt to fetch, copy, or reorganise them'). The upstream crate is 55328 lines.

So there are two positions and the workspace currently holds neither cleanly:
 (A) Keep vendoring. Then outram-foam-basic-lib must NEVER become a Cargo dependency of tampines-steam-tables, and shared numerics (the golden section, and anything like it) get duplicated by design. The duplication op-uyi3 found is then expected, not a defect, and the rule should say so.
 (B) Depend on it. Then the 23489 vendored lines should be deleted and imported instead, which is a large, testable change touching the Edwards blowdown path. Dependency-wise this is cheap: outram-foam-basic-lib's default features pull only thiserror+uom+ndarray, all of which tampines-steam-tables already has, and rayon/wgpu are off by default with wgpu target-gated off Android. Android-buildability is NOT an obstacle.

Nobody has decided. Until someone does, agents will keep re-proposing the promotion and keep being told no, or worse, will add the dependency and produce a build containing the same crate twice.

Deliverable: a maintainer decision recorded in crates/tampines-steam-tables/CLAUDE.md, stating which of A or B holds and why.
title: tampines-steam-tables vendors outram-foam-basic-lib AND could depend on it: decide which

description:
After the conus landed, k = 1.040984 +/- 0.001148 = +3670 pcm vs RMC 1.004288.
The old -909 pcm was two offsetting errors. Find the over-reactive one.

PREDICTIONS MADE BEFORE MEASURING (sign, rough magnitude):

A. Discharge tube (r<25 below conus floor) is reflector graphite; really a
   tube of pebbles/void. Replace with helium -> LESS reflection at the conus
   tip -> k DOWN. Predict -200 to -800 pcm.

B. Control-rod borings (r 95.6-108.6) solid graphite. 10 channels of 13 cm
   dia at r=102.1 -> boring area 10*pi*6.5^2 = 1327 cm2 of annulus area
   pi*(108.6^2-95.6^2) = 8340 cm2 = 15.9 % void. Homogenising removes
   graphite -> k DOWN. Predict -100 to -400 pcm.

C. Symmetric bottom: 229 cm graphite below the conus. Overlaps A; the real
   model has the discharge tube through it. Predict small once A is in.

D. Conus packing uses bulk 0.61; pebbles on a sloping wall pack worse
   (~0.55-0.58). Less fuel -> k DOWN. Conus is 13.6 % of fuel volume, so an
   8 % packing cut is ~1 % of total fuel. Predict -300 to -600 pcm.

E. Every reflector region a single homogenised TECDOC zone. Direction
   unknown until the zone map is read.

F. NOT ON THE LIST, found while reading: the SourceBox is [-50,50]^3 and the
   entropy mesh [-60,60]^3, but the bed now reaches conus_floor = -98.2 cm.
   Both miss the conus. Source box should not matter after 30-40 inactive
   generations; the entropy mesh being blind to the conus DOES make the
   convergence diagnostic unreliable. Predict source box ~0 pcm (test it),
   entropy mesh a diagnostic fix not a k fix.

Sum of predicted candidates is roughly -600 to -1800 pcm against a +3670
residual, so the predictions do NOT close it. Stated in advance.
title: HTR-10 +3670 pcm residual: find the error the absent conus was masking

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
Groundwork for this bead was written 2026-08-11 and is sitting UNCOMMITTED in the working tree — crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/properties.rs, +556 lines. Not backed up anywhere else. Recording it here so it is not mistaken for un-started work.

WHAT LANDED IN THE TREE:
- IF97 range constants pulled out as named public items: T_MAX_REGION_1 623.15 K, T_MAX_REGION_2 1073.15 K, T_MIN_IF97 273.16 K.
- Metastability limits: MAX_METASTABLE_LIQUID_SUPERHEAT 30.0 K, MAX_METASTABLE_VAPOUR_SUBCOOLING 30.0 K. These are the thermal-non-equilibrium excursion caps the six-equation model needs and the drift-flux/HEM models do not.
- SaturatedTransport { at(p), is_stale_for(p), liquid_prandtl(..), vapour_prandtl(..), liquid_conductivity(), vapour_conductivity(), check_same_pressure(..) } with TRANSPORT_CACHE_TOLERANCE 1.0e-2 — a per-pressure transport-property cache with a staleness test, so the interfacial heat-transfer closures do not re-flash IF97 transport every cell every step.
- PhaseState { liquid_at(p,h,saturated), vapour_at(p,h,saturated), thermodynamic_temperature(), mass_density() } — the per-phase (not mixture) thermodynamic state the six-equation energy equations march.
- Helpers check_flash_inputs(..) and invert_monotone_fast(..).

STATE: compiles; `cargo test --release -p tampines --lib multiphase_1d` -> 6 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored. None of those 6 exercises the new types — there is no TwoFluid1d solver to consume them yet, and two_fluid_tests.rs is still the 12-line placeholder registered so the module map stays stable.

CAUTION for whoever picks this up: TRANSPORT_CACHE_TOLERANCE = 1.0e-2 is a 1 % relative pressure window for reusing cached transport properties. That is an accuracy/speed trade nobody has measured the error of. Before the solver depends on it, quantify what a 1 % pressure staleness does to mu and k near the saturation line, where they vary fastest — or make the tolerance a documented, justified number rather than a chosen one.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
SOLVER CORE IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12. crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/two_fluid.rs went from a 139-line scaffold whose step() returned NotYetImplemented to a working six-equation semi-implicit march (+2493 lines); two_fluid_tests.rs from a 12-line placeholder with zero tests to 18 verification tests (+1950 lines).

NOTE ON THIS BEAD'S TITLE: it says 'interfacial-pressure regularisation'. That is WRONG and was written before the source study. OpenFOAM's multiphaseEuler contains NO interfacial-pressure term at all -- no pInterface, no Stuhmiller, no Bestion, anywhere in the vendored tree (six-equation-regularisation.md section 1). What is implemented instead is VIRTUAL MASS folded inside the implicit 2x2 phase-coupling block, plus residualAlpha flooring, which is what upstream actually does for a fluid-fluid pair.

WHAT WAS BUILT:
- PhaseCouplingBlock / PhaseCouplingInputs: the 2x2 implicit drag + virtual-mass block per face, inverted in closed form. det = A_g A_l + A_g c_l + A_l c_g, a sum of non-negative terms, so it cannot lose its sign to cancellation and is strictly positive wherever residual-alpha flooring holds the diagonals up.
- Pressure equation derived from the VOLUME CONSTRAINT (sum of the phase continuity equations each divided by rho_k), so the flashing appears as a volumetric source Gamma (1/rho_g - 1/rho_l) and there is no kink to linearise across -- unlike drift flux, no secant is needed.
- Outer correctors are a proper Newton iteration on the volume residual R = alpha_g + alpha_l - 1, with the quasi-Jacobian -(V/dt) dR/dp assembled once per step. The first draft mixed a linearisation about p_old with a Newton correction and STALLED at R ~ 1e-4; fixed.
- Compressibilities taken along the ISENTROPIC path dh_k = dp/rho_k rather than at fixed enthalpy, because the energy equation applies the work term in the same step. Using the fixed-enthalpy derivative was measured to stall the correctors.
- Interfacial heat transfer solved IMPLICITLY in the phase enthalpies (closed form Q = dT/(1/K + dt/(m cp))), which is unconditionally stable and self-limiting.
- Conserved primary state is (m_g, m_l, m_g h_g, m_l h_l); alpha and rho are derived. Nothing is renormalised: the volume residual is reported and refused above 1e-4.

HONESTY: the regularisation is documented as TRACED TO UPSTREAM PRACTICE and explicitly NOT proven to restore hyperbolicity. No characteristic analysis was done, here or upstream, and two upstream tutorials run with no regularising term at all.

FOLLOW-UP BEADS FILED (7): the tampines-steam-tables Region-4 panic (P1); the low-void expansion-work refusal that BLOCKS a two-fluid Edwards case; the undiagnosed corrector non-convergence at small bubble diameter; the missing Dirichlet-pressure boundaries; the measured drift-flux/two-fluid compressibility disagreement; the virtual-mass port into outram-foam-multiphase; and performance.

ONE FILE OUTSIDE THE ASSIGNED SCOPE WAS TOUCHED: edwards_tests.rs::two_fluid_step_still_refuses_to_pretend asserted step() returns NotYetImplemented and could not compile against the new constructor signature. It was rewritten into two_fluid_constructs_on_the_edwards_geometry, which asserts only construction, and its doc comment records the change. That test's own docs had always described itself as the placeholder to replace when the solver landed.

title: tampines: TwoFluid1d solver core — six-eqn semi-implicit march, traced drag + interfacial heat transfer, interfacial-pressure regularisation

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
PORTED MODULES DONE and committed as 9483d1d5: 183 variable-index sites converted, gate added, 304 tests green, all four cross-target builds clean.

UPSTREAM HALF, in progress. The count of sites in the lifts is 62, not the 42 I estimated on op-chyp -- that estimate is withdrawn; 62 is what the same rule the gate applies actually finds. They sit in 6 of the 19 lifted files, from two upstreams:
  outram-foam-basic-lib   square_matrix.rs 33, polynomial/polynomial.rs 5, polynomial/roots.rs 2
  chem-eng (z_domain)     conversion.rs 11, polynomial.rs 7, discrete_tf.rs 4

SquareMatrix turned out to exist in FIVE byte-identical copies -- outram-foam-basic-lib, tampines-steam-tables, teh-o-prke, tuas_boussinesq_solver and outram-park-fork-coolprop. Only the doc comments differ; the lu_decompose/lu_back_substitute/solve bodies are identical across all five. Fixing one would have introduced drift where there is none today, so the same patch went to all five. Worth a bead of its own: five copies of a dense LU is five places for a fix to be forgotten.

SEMANTIC CHANGES THE MAINTAINER SHOULD REVIEW, because they are not pure refactors:
  - SquareMatrix::get and Roots::get return NaN for an out-of-range index instead of panicking; set/add discard an out-of-range write; Index<usize> for Roots borrows a shared NaN. Previously each was a loud panic at the bug site. On a desktop crate that panic was useful; the trade buys petir its bare-metal guarantee. All five copies changed together.
  - lu_back_substitute returns early, leaving b partly updated, when pivot or b is shorter than n. Also previously a panic.
Both are documented at the call site and in each method's doc comment.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: reactingTwoPhaseEulerFoam application solver landed (commit 35a4de8). Upstream reactingTwoPhaseEulerFoam is folded into OpenFOAM-dev's runtime-selectable multiphaseEuler module (applications/modules/multiphaseEuler); ported its loop structure + reacting-two-phase physics as ReactingTwoPhaseEulerFoam in src/solvers/reacting_two_phase_euler_foam/. Per the Layer-5 rule it composes the hydrodynamic core from outram-foam-multiphase (TwoFluidPimple: two momentum predictors + shared-pressure PISO + drag + alpha transport) and adds the app layer mirroring multiphaseEuler.C's thermophysicalPredictor: per-phase conservative enthalpy eqns (heEqn form, alpha-rho weighted, kappa/Cp diffusion), one-resistance interfacial heat transfer (Spherical/Ranz-Marshall/constant-Nu, K=6 max(alpha_d,alpha_res) kappa_c Nu/d^2), operator-split interfacial mass transfer (phase change) + latent heat, and a volumetric reaction heat source. Added outram-foam-multiphase to root+applib deps. Enum dispatch, no dyn/lifetimes, uom boundary, GPLv3+OpenFOAM provenance. Verification-tested only (Nusselt exactness; thermal equilibration to mass-heat-weighted mean, <1% energy conservation; closed reaction heat-up vs analytic; phase-change alpha shift) -- NO benchmark validation (human V&V). 269 applib lib tests pass, zero warnings. Honest scope: constant Cp/kappa, no species/finite-rate chemistry (reaction=prescribed volumetric heat), one-resistance HT, operator-split phase change, no population balance/MRF/LTS/p_rgh.

title: outram-foam-appbuilder-lib — solver/app builder + GeN-Foam host

Then quantify: closed beads by type, introduction-to-detection interval, found-by human vs test vs agent vs external oracle. State the n=1 limit early.
title: Paper 3: mine the bead + commit corpus for the defect taxonomy

description: The CoolProp port (outram_park_fork_coolprop::humid_air) can output HumidAirParam::TWetBulb, but tampines::humid_air::HumidAirState has no wet-bulb field and tampines does not re-export ha_props. Consequence: outram-park-digital-twin-engine's CoolingTowerVisual cannot obtain the wet-bulb temperature that governs a cooling tower (approach = T_water,out - T_wb); it is taken as a caller-supplied scalar in CoolingTowerScalars::inlet_wet_bulb instead. Computing it inside the digital-twin engine would be new physics in a presentation crate, which that crate's CLAUDE.md forbids. Fix belongs in tampines: add t_wet_bulb (and probably t_dew_point) to HumidAirState, resolved through ha_props like the other eight fields. Found 2026-08-12 while building the cooling-tower artwork.
title: tampines::humid_air: expose wet-bulb temperature on HumidAirState
